The overview says what the group is doing, and an instance can be started, stopped and watched.

## ✨ Added

- **A summary above the instance list.** The cards each said what one box was doing and nothing said what the group was doing: how many instances answered, how many files are queued across all of them, how much is left, and how fast it is all going. It carries one play/stop badge for the whole group, and the badge follows the group's state rather than offering both — "start" only when every instance that answered is halted, because a single running instance means the group is not stopped.
- **Start, stop and a speed graph inside an instance.** The queue was a switch, which says on/off about a thing whose verbs are start and stop; it is the same state-following badge the summary uses. The graph appears only while something is actually moving and is scaled to the tallest sample in its own window, so a home connection and a gigabit one both see their own shape — the absolute number sits in the line above it.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The instance cards show what the instance is doing, not where the connection goes.** They printed the relay address, which is the same for every card in the list, so it distinguished nothing while occupying the one line that could have. Same four figures, same order, as the browser extension's own card.
- **Removing a connection lives inside the instance**, not on every row of a list you tap to open. A bin on each row is a mis-tap waiting to happen, and it competed with the only action the row actually has.
- **The back control in the settings is a real target.** It was a single "‹", so the tappable area was the size of that character — about 12 by 22 points against the 44 both platforms ask for.
- **The gear is filled.** It was the text glyph U+2699, which every system font draws as a thin outline: a line-drawn glyph among filled badges and filled switches is the one thing the design language's icon rule rules out.
- **Accent label left, swatches right, one row**, matching the web interface's own colour card and every other row on the page.
- **The version footer**, build plus GlimStone, the same quiet line the web interface and the extension carry.
- **Tablets get a readable column width.** The layout was one column stretched edge to edge, so a card on a 10" screen ran 900 points wide with its text at one edge and its badge at the other. Capped and centred; a phone is unaffected, since the cap is wider than every phone.

## 🐞 Fixed

- **The light theme still resolved to the retired dark yellow.** Nobody ever picked `#8E6A00` — it was the light theme's accent back when one token did both jobs, and switching "follow the instance" off snapshots the *resolved* look into the override layer, so the retired default got frozen into storage as if it were a choice. A stored value the picker cannot produce is not a preference; it is dropped on load.

## 📋 Notes

- Eight strings arrived in all 42 languages, one left with the relay line it replaced.
